newsitem.title: USA: Stocks fall after housing report fuels rate fears.
newsitem.headline: Stocks fall after housing report fuels rate fears.

text.p: Stocks fell sharply Tuesday as a surprisingly strong report on the housing market reignited fears that the Federal Reserve would raise interest rates in a bid to ward off inflation.

The Dow Jones industrial average lost 58.92 points to 6,896.56 after falling 100 points earlier in the session. In the broader market, declining issues beat advances 1,643 to 844 on active volume of 467 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.

A government report that housing starts rose 12.2 percent in February to the fastest rate in nearly three years further worried investors that Fed policy-makers would raise short-term rates at their meeting on March 25 to slow the economy's growth.
While the jump in housing starts was aided by unusually warm weather, the robust activity still surprised economists.
"Even adjusting for seasonal flukiness, the housing sector is doing extremely well," said David Wyss, an economist at DRI/McGraw Hill Inc.
"This market is obsessed with March 25," said Jack Shaughnessy, director of research at Advest. "The strong housing numbers this morning contributed to that."
He said the stock market appeared prepared for a marginal increase of a quarter point in short-term rates, but "there's a fear there might be even more of an increase."
With several major reports to come before the meeting of central bank policy-makers, analysts said volatility was only going to increase in the days ahead.

"We've got the (Consumer Price Index) tomorrow, triple witching on Friday and the Fed next week," said Alfred Goldman, technical analyst at A.G. Edwards & Sons. "Until the Fed drops the other shoe or puts it back on its foot, this market is going to stay whippy."

Banking shares were among the hardest hit by the interest rate jitters, with J.P. Morgan & Co. off 3-3/8 to 105, the steepest decline among Dow index components. Chase Manhattan Corp. fell 3-1/4 to 99-1/2 and Wells Fargo & Co. dipped 5-3/4 to 297-1/8.
Among individual issues, Wolverine Tube fell 7-7/8 to 26 after the company warned that its first quarter profits would be below year-ago levels.
Harman International Industries was another victim of an earnings warning, as it skidded 11-3/4 to 34-1/4 after saying quarterly results would fall sharply from a year earlier.

Zenith Electronics jumped 2-1/2 to 12 on news that Time Warner Inc.'s cable television unit would use Zenith's set-top boxes as part of a service enhancement in some of its markets. Time Warner rose 1/2 to 43-1/2.
The Nasdaq Composite index fell 10.09 points to 1,269.34.
The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks fell 6.05 to 789.66. The American Stock Exchange index slipped 0.79 to 595.45.
The NYSE composite index of all listed common stocks fell 2.97 to 415.40. The average share was down 31 cents.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was 7,517.895, down 58.778 or 0.78 percent.
